scope: Additive Home Village TH18 Super Hog Rider Divide and Conquer integration. All earlier frozen references remain unmodified.
game_version: The immutable upstream payload is commit 62b019df868f9decb49e97a0ff5ae15fb27af9ba. Supercell's June 2023 launch table gives the parent and child L10-L12 values. A current secondary table supplies child L13-L15 values but does not identify an immutable client build.

sources.title: New Super Troop
sources.limitations: The official launch note establishes the death split, Super Hog defense targeting and wall jump, Super Rider nearest-building targeting, ground-only single-target attacks, movement speeds, Rider 2x wall damage, and the parent and child L10-L12 HP and DPS tables. It does not give L13-L15 child values, spawn timing, launch geometry, target inheritance, collision or a current client build.

sources.title: Super Hog Rider/Super Hog and Super Hog Rider/Super Rider
sources.limitations: The current public tables report child L10-L15 HP, DPS, damage per hit, range and cadence, and record the L13, L14 and L15 additions. The companion Super Hog page provides the equivalent Hog values. Neither page identifies a capture build or exact child launch coordinates.

support.note: Core queues one Super Hog and one Super Rider at the death tick through the shared value-only spawn path. Parent L10-L12 values are primary. L13-L15 child values are secondary.

changed_values.previous_state: Catalogued-only parent with no Core Kind or split lifecycle. Its pinned raw L12 HP was 1750.
changed_values.replacement: Parent L10-L12 values use Supercell's launch table, correcting L12 HP to 1700. Destruction now produces one non-deployable Super Hog and one non-deployable Super Rider at the same matched level.
changed_values.justification: The official launch note directly publishes the corrected parent L12 HP and the split contract. Hashed secondary observations provide L13-L15 child data without replacing the frozen source payload.

known_uncertainties: Supercell does not publish L13-L15 child values. Those values are secondary and the external table does not identify a current client build.

The public documentation describes the Rider launch only as several tiles backwards. It does not publish exact direction, distance, delay, collision, target inheritance or tick ordering. Core deterministically queues both children at the deceased parent's position on the death tick.
The Super Hog wall jump is established, but its exact pathing and collision contract is not. It therefore uses the shared ground path route and is not presented as wall-jump fidelity.
The Viewer receives the child entities from Core but has no separately source-verified child asset or launch animation. No placeholder is marked as an asset-complete result.
conclusion: Super Hog Rider is executable through shared Core, CLI, Viewer and RL paths with a primary-established split and source-backed child tables. It remains partial until child launch, wall-jump, distraction and visual contracts are versioned.
